newsitem.title: USA: San Jose group makes pitch for Oakland A's - report.
newsitem.headline: San Jose group makes pitch for Oakland A's - report.

text.p: The San Jose Sports Authority has approached the Oakland Athletics about the possibility of building a new stadium for the baseball team in the San Jose area, the San Francisco Chronicle reported Thursday.
The newspaper did not give a source for the report.
The Oakland Athletics had no immediate comment and no one was available to comment at the San Jose Sports Authority, which organizes sporting events in San Jose.
The success of the San Jose Sharks hockey team has whetted the appetite of civic leaders in the area for more sports teams, the Chronicle said.

Oakland A's owners Steve Schott and Ken Hofmann have a lease with the Oakland Coliseum that gives them the option of leaving after next season. Both have hinted that they would be prepared to move the team elsewhere in the San Francisco Bay area if a new stadium were available, the report said.
But it said any effort to build the Athletics a state-of-the-art ballpark in the San Jose area would face numerous obstacles.
Suitable land is scarce in San Jose. Any facility would need to be funded at least in part by public money and area voters defeated ballpark initiatives in 1990 and 1992, it said.

The report said Major League Baseball had an agreement with the San Francisco Giants that Santa Clara County, which comprises San Jose, was Giants' territory. The Chronicle quoted several sources as saying baseball could be expected to block any attempt by the A's to move to San Jose.
